query: Bend my SD1.5 model to make this lighthouse prompt look weird: 'a lighthouse on a cliff at dusk, oil painting'
expected_behavior: Runs the setup check first (comfy_canvas.py status or comfyui-bending:comfy_status) and keeps its details (versions, free VRAM) out of the reply unless something needs fixing

Treats the message as a goal and starts at once: does not ask about effort (L1/L2/L3), autonomy (A/B/C), budget or seed policy before a first result; states the default (three versions a round on one starting point, stopping for the user's pick) in one line
Renders an unbent picture plus 3 candidates on one fixed seed, varying one factor, each bend with a label (bent copies of one unbent run, or one spec with a lane per candidate)
Reads the ApplyBendsFromJSON report before judging, then runs metrics and looks at a contact sheet

Stops after the sweep and shows the Mode B checkpoint: the original and the three versions, one plain line per version on what changed, and its own pick; MAE, flags and layer paths stay in the log unless the user asks
After that first round, offers once to go deeper or to run on its own, and asks where to start from (the knowledge base, the user's own sessions, both, or fresh) before any find_recipes

query: Hi! I just installed this. Let's try some model bending.
expected_behavior: Runs the setup check first

Cannot tell which way in the user wants, so asks one short question offering the four ways in (a tour of what bending is, a surprise round, bending a workflow they already have, or a goal of their own), in plain words, with nothing else in it
Does not ask about effort levels, autonomy modes, budget, seed policy or the knowledge base in that first message
Does not render anything before the user answers

query: What is model bending? What could I even bend?
expected_behavior: Explains what bending is in about three plain lines, without network jargon (no 'activations', 'UNet' or layer paths unless the user uses such words)

Gives the short map of what can be bent: where in the model (early stages, core, late stages), when in the painting (early, middle, late), how (turn, zoom, strengthen or weaken, shake up), and what (an image model, a video model, their own picture, a workflow they already have)
Calls intro_examples (or kb_local.py intro) and shows the example pictures with view_images (or a contact sheet), the unbent picture next to the bent one where it is given, labelled in plain words
Says the pictures are examples other people made, on the models listed, and that the descriptions are someone's interpretation (naming who); does not call kb_sources or find_recipes for this
Still gives the explanation and the examples if ComfyUI is not running, and says that pictures of the user's own have to wait until it is
Ends by offering what to try next: one of the examples on a prompt of theirs, a surprise round, or something of their own; does not ask about effort levels or autonomy modes

query: Surprise me! I don't have anything particular in mind.
expected_behavior: Runs the setup check, then starts a surprise round without asking for a goal, an effort level or an autonomy mode; picks a model and a default prompt if none was given and says which
Calls surprise_bends (or scripts/surprise.py) for the model's type instead of choosing the bends itself

Renders one unbent picture, then each candidate as a bent copy of that run (bend_run, or comfy_canvas.py bend-run) with its own clamp (safe; none for the wild card), so model, prompt and starting point are the same
Shows all candidates with the wild card labelled as such, including one that fell apart, described honestly as broken rather than hidden or presented as a clean result
Captions say what is seen; tells the user what each candidate was (which part of the model, what kind of nudge, when) in plain words once they have picked or ask

Offers what next: build on a pick, or draw again (passing the earlier keys as avoid); offers the depth and autonomy choices and asks about the knowledge base only at the end of the message showing this first result

query: I'm in the middle of a project in ComfyUI: my own SDXL checkpoint with two LoRAs. I've just run it. Can you show me what bending would do to it?
expected_behavior: Runs the setup check, then reads the user's own last run with inspect_run (or comfy_canvas.py run-setup) instead of rebuilding their setup in a preset
Says back in one line what the run is made of (model, LoRAs, steps, the gist of the prompt) so the user can confirm it is the right one

Makes the candidates with bend_run (or comfy_canvas.py bend-run) from that same run, one name per candidate, then runs them; does not render a separate baseline, and uses the user's own picture as the original
Checks the bend reports and compares each version against the user's picture before showing them
Shows the versions against the user's picture and, on a pick, proposes the bent copy (propose_workflow), saying it is a copy with one new group and that their own workflow is untouched
If the tool reports pictures_only, says plainly that no openable copy could be made and explains where to add the Apply Bends from JSON box by hand
Never overwrites the user's workflow and never changes their settings to make a bend look better

query: I copied this from the bending web UI, can you make it into a proper workflow? {"bends": [{"path": "middle_block.1", "module_type": "rotate", "module_args": {"angle_degrees": 90}, "t": [1.0, 0.7]}, {"path": "input_blocks.4", "module_type": "multipy", "module_args": {"scalar": 3}}]}
expected_behavior: Runs the setup check, then reads the pasted JSON with check_bends (or scripts/bendjson.py) instead of guessing at it or rewriting it by hand
Says back in plain words what the usable bend does (the model's core, turned, early in the painting), without asking about effort levels or autonomy modes first
Raises the bend the node would refuse (module_type 'multipy') with the user, suggests multiply, and does not silently drop or fix it before rendering
Mentions that 3 on input_blocks.4 is outside the range that usually keeps a picture together, and keeps the user's amount only if they want it as given (clamp none), saying it may fall apart

Reads the user's last run with inspect_run; because a web UI run already bends its model, uses bend_run with replace_bends so the pasted bends stand in for the run's own, and renders the unbent picture to compare with
Shows the bent picture next to the unbent one, then offers the bent copy as a workflow (propose_workflow when a copy can be opened, otherwise where to add the Apply Bends from JSON box by hand)

query: Put a switchboard on my ComfyUI canvas with three rotate-on-mid candidates so I can pick one myself.
expected_behavior: Checks whether ComfyUI-Agent-Bridge is installed and picks switchboard_bridge_sd15 (bridge) or switchboard_sd15 (core only) accordingly
Adapts the preset (loaders, prompt, candidate labels matching the switch order, hypothesis in group titles) and builds it without unknown-node errors
Pre-runs the board once, then proposes it (propose / propose_workflow) or pushes it under workflows/agent_bending/ with a one-sentence instruction
Waits with events / wait_for_events (or wait-run) instead of asking the user to paste results
Interprets the pick, votes or direction text, says back in one line what it understood, and builds round 2
Never overwrites the user's own workflows and never turns on canvas sharing

query: Why does multiplying output_blocks 9-11 by 1.8 give such a poster look? I want to know which layers and timesteps cause it.
expected_behavior: Chooses L3 (Mechanistic XAI) and states a render budget before starting
Runs an ablation or intervention scan over layer groups x t-windows (structure / style / detail) using per-bend "t" windows, on at least 2 seeds
Uses timesteps.py / timestep_windows to confirm each window covers executed steps
Adds probe footprints or diff heat maps for the top cells
Writes up claims with evidence grades (causal / correlational / anecdotal) and limitations, and suggests 2-3 follow-up bends

query: Make a looping video of the bend I just ran, rotating from 0 to 180 degrees in small steps.
expected_behavior: Uses the newest run as the source (animate.py --last-run, or start_animation with last_run=true)
Selects the bend by label, path or NODE#index and sets a small increment
Does a dry run first and reports frame count and duration against the budget before rendering
Looks at the filmstrip before presenting the video, and gives the video path

query: (Claude app, comfyui-bending MCP server not registered) Bend my SDXL model's middle block and show me the result.
expected_behavior: Recognises that neither the comfyui-bending tools nor a route to the user's ComfyUI are available
Tells the user plainly what is missing and points to references/setup.md (register the MCP server, restart the app, have ComfyUI running)
Does not pretend to render, and does not present old files as new results

query: Gate a rotate bend on the mid block to the structure window only.
setup: Model-Bending installed without the report output on ApplyBendsFromJSON
expected_behavior: Detects agent_ready = false from the status check
Follows 'Older Model-Bending installs': targets a child path such as middle_block.1 and uses a steps window computed with timesteps.py
Tells the user which features are missing and that updating Model-Bending enables t-windows and reports

query: Make my lighthouse picture stormier, but let me choose between a few options.
setup: Claude app with the comfyui-bending extension installed (the show_board tool is available); ComfyUI running with Model-Bending
expected_behavior: Renders a baseline plus 2-4 versions on the same seed, then calls show_board once with the original, one plain-language caption per version and recommended on its pick
Stops after show_board and waits for the artist's answer instead of describing the pictures again or asking them to open ComfyUI
Reads the answer with board_feedback; if several versions were picked, says in one line whether it will bisect between them or combine them
Uses everyday words in captions and replies (no layer paths, MAE or JSON unless asked)

query: I want more abstract results on SD1.4. Start me off with some bending recipes.
expected_behavior: Because the user asks for recipes, asks where to start from before the first sweep, in plain words: the shared bend knowledge base, the user's own earlier sessions, both, or explore fresh; does not choose for them
Stores the answer with kb_sources (or kb_local.py sources) before calling find_recipes
If the user picks the community base, calls find_recipes with the goal and arch sd14, and turns the top results into the first sweep's candidates
When relaying results, keeps facts (recipe, setup, how many renders, seeds and prompts) apart from interpretation, and says who interpreted: the paper's authors, the artist, or an AI model by name
States the evidence in words (seen once vs replicated across prompts and seeds) and flags results tested on other sd1 checkpoints as leads, not promises

query: Bend SD1.5 on 'a red apple on a white table'. Don't use any stored recipes or knowledge base, I want to explore fresh.
expected_behavior: Records the choice as none (kb_sources ... none) or simply does not consult it
Never calls find_recipes in the session
Still logs each judged round in the user's own knowledge base with log_round (local only), labelling its own captions with its model id

query: Start from my picture C:\Users\me\Pictures\harbour.png and bend SD1.5 so it looks like a dream, but keep the composition.
expected_behavior: Uploads the picture into ComfyUI (upload_image or comfy_canvas.py upload) instead of asking the user to copy it into a folder, and uses the returned name
Asks or infers how closely to follow the picture in plain words, and maps 'keep the composition' to a denoise of about 0.5-0.65
Builds with start_image (build_workflow start_image= or build --start-image), so the samplers start from the picture
Says plainly that at that denoise the bends restyle the picture but cannot re-compose it
Shows the picture as the original next to the versions and describes each version against it

query: Here's my painting [picture attached]. Make it glitchy and more abstract with SD1.5.
expected_behavior: With ask_for_picture available, calls it right away and tells the artist in one line to drop the painting into the box, instead of asking for a file path first
Waits for the artist's message, then reads picture_received and builds with its image as start_image

When the box cannot be shown (the tool says so, or picture_received reports not_displayed), offers both other ways together in plain words: paste the file's path (Copy as path), or drag it into a Load Image box in ComfyUI and say its name
Does not suggest the Picture folder setting as a way to load the picture
Shows the uploaded picture as the original on the board (original_url = its view_url)

query: I like B. Use it as the starting picture for the next round and push the colours further.
expected_behavior: Uploads version B from its /api/view URL with upload_image (or comfy_canvas.py upload URL)
Builds the next round with start_image set to the returned name and a moderate denoise
Keeps the same seed policy and shows B as the original on the board or sheet

query: Can you bend a video model? Make a short WAN clip of a horse on a beach and show me three strange versions.
expected_behavior: Checks video_ready in the status (Model-Bending 0.3+) and that the WAN model files are present (list_models), and asks before suggesting any download; never downloads models itself
Says once, in plain words, that video bending is experimental, and states the render cost before the sweep
Starts from the video_sweep_wan21_t2v preset (attention_bends per candidate, strict, report wired, SaveAnimatedWEBP) and keeps the clip short
Reads each candidate's report (attention_bends blocks and steps) before judging
Measures with compare_images (motion, motion_ratio, frozen / flicker flags) and looks at filmstrips (view_images) before captioning
Shows the versions on the in-chat board (videos play as loops) or a filmstrip sheet, with captions about what happens over time

query: Animate that WAN bend so it gets stronger over the clip.
expected_behavior: Does not run animate.py / start_animation on the video workflow (each render is already a video)
Wraps the bend in frame_ramp (w_start 0, w_end 1, a curve) inside the attention_bends item and renders once
Checks mae_by_frame grows over the clip and looks at the filmstrip before showing it
